problem.concept: massive amounts of sequencing data continues to overwhelm the processing capability of existing algorithms and compute infrastructures.

task.concept: reduce the execution time of short sequence alignment

method.concept: hardware accelerator that adopts modern FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) architectures

contribution.concept: Shouji
hardware accelerator
Shouji significantly improves the accuracy of pre-alignment filtering by up to two orders of magnitude compared to the state-of-the-art pre-alignment filters, GateKeeper and SHD.
Our FPGA-based accelerator is up to three orders of magnitude faster than the equivalent CPU implementation of Shouji.

Using a single FPGA chip: five state-of-the-art sequence aligners, designed for different computing platforms. The addition of Shouji as a pre-alignment step reduces the execution time of the five state-of-the-art sequence aligners by up to 18.8x.
Shouji does not sacrifice any of the aligner capabilities, as it does not modify or replace the alignment step.
